title: Heart of Glass (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded at the Record Plant, New York, June 1978, produced by Mike Chapman, built on a Roland CR-78 combined with live drums, "the bass drum recorded separately from the rest of the drums" (after BBC Radio 2's The Record Producers, 25 May 2009). The single remix accentuates the double-tracked bass drum.

title: Dreaming (Blondie song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded live in the studio (Jimmy Destri). Burke: "That take of 'Dreaming' was just me kind of blowing through the song ... I was consciously overplaying just for the sake of it because it was a run-through." Stewart Mason (AllMusic): "possibly the most over-the-top effort by a rock & roll drummer in the entire 1970s". Played on Saturday Night Live in 1979, Burke jumping over his kit at the end.

title: Atomic (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Written by Debbie Harry and Jimmy Destri, produced by Mike Chapman; "a mixture of new wave, rock and disco". The 4:35 album version has the "Three Blind Mice" intro and a bass solo that the 7" remix (February 1980) replaces.

title: Clem Burke in depth: Blondie drummer on legacy, the new album, Eurythmics, Ramones and more (MusicRadar, 2014)
notes: For Blondie's 40th anniversary. "A Moonie-style red sparkle Premier" (the writer). "Heart Of Glass was played to a drum machine"; "I never played to a click in the studio with all the Blondie stuff"; a Simmons kit with his acoustic kit in Eurythmics. Influences: "Top 40 radio in the US, The Four Seasons, The Young Rascals, The Beatles ... Hal Blaine and Earl Palmer ... Al Jackson, Keith Moon and Ringo Starr". The Saturday Night Fever and ABBA behind Heart of Glass; Chic behind Rapture.

title: How to do pop "the right way": an interview with Clem Burke of Blondie (Paul French, Mixdown, 17 April 2024)
notes: "The snare on all that early Blondie stuff is all the stock 14" x 6.5" wooden Premier snare that came with the kit"; "Usually Remo Ambassadors"; a 24" kick and a red sparkle kit (the writer). Heart of Glass "took a very long time to record ... up until that point we had never played to a click track. I had to lay a sort of a click track with the kick to the arpeggiator on a very early Roland Synthesizer, which was constantly going out of sync." Read through a summarising fetch; the page refuses plain requests.

title: Profiles: Clem Burke (Beat It, 23 April 2025)
notes: A profile after his death, quoting his interviews: his father a club drummer; the St Andrew's Bridgemen Drum and Bugle Corps ("I actually wound up on rudimental bass drum"); left-handed on a right-handed kit, his right hand leading but "he would start fills with his left hand, just like Ringo Starr does"; a Premier loaner kit on the early UK tours, then the endorsement (Live From My Drum Room); Hal Blaine and Earl Palmer "consummate studio musicians"; Kraftwerk an influence on Heart of Glass.

title: Clem Burke: Eat to the Beat (New Directions in Music, 2025)
notes: A listener's appreciation after his death: "His paradiddling across floor toms and snare" in Dreaming, "a rumbling bottom"; fills that "owe a lot to Keith Moon, but there is more precision"; Atomic's "bristling human energy".
